children: Shares of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited are trading lower on Friday morning, falling 2.12 per cent to ₹965.20 by 10.45 AM, even as the company reported its highest-ever half-yearly profit a day earlier.

The stock opened at ₹1,001, briefly touching a session high of ₹1,005.35, before retreating sharply to an intraday low of ₹956, suggesting selling pressure emerged after the initial post-result optimism. The previous close was ₹986.10.

Traded volume stood at 7.25 lakh shares with a turnover of ₹70.60 crore by mid-morning, indicating active participation. Buy orders outweigh sell orders at 58.68 per cent versus 41.32 per cent, though the price decline reflects overhead supply. Deliverable trades account for 39.82 per cent of total volume.

The results, announced on October 29, showed Q2FY27 Operating PAT rising 29 per cent year-on-year to ₹718 crore. The company’s H1FY27 Total PAT, including Other Comprehensive Income, came in at ₹2,583 crore, up 51 per cent year-on-year. Asset Management was the standout segment, with PAT jumping 69 per cent YoY to ₹304 crore. Annual Recurring Revenue now contributes 66 per cent of total revenue.

The stock trades at a P/E of 22 and carries a market capitalisation of ₹58,075 crore. It remains well off its 52-week high of ₹1,090.25, hit on October 7, 2026. The 52-week low was ₹614.90 in March 2026.

On a longer horizon, the stock has returned 279.62 per cent over three years and 320.71 per cent over five years, significantly outpacing broader indices. Year-to-date returns stand at 14.45 per cent.
The intraday pullback appears consistent with a “sell on news” pattern following yesterday’s strong results, a common occurrence when positive outcomes are already priced in.

title: Motilal Oswal shares slip despite record half-year profit; stock down 2% in early trade
